subject: Pegasus Analytics — throughput drop & 5xx spike (war-room coordination)
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@pegasus.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anika D'Souza <anika@pegasus.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:47:12 -0800
Subject: Unexpected latency & 502s on inference calls

Karthik —

We started seeing a sharp drop in throughput around 08:15 PST and a spike of 502/503 responses across multiple endpoints. Tail latency for our user-facing path has jumped from ~120ms to >1.5s. Attached are a small set of traces and a compressed set of logs (pegasus_error_logs_1130.tar.gz).

This is impacting our payment verification flow; our ops team is blocking traffic to keep error rates down. Can you confirm this is on your side and what the ETA is for a fix?

Samir
VP Engineering, Pegasus Analytics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@pegasus.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:56:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency & 502s on inference calls

Samir — thanks for the report and the logs. I've looped in our infra and customer success leads to triage immediately.

Quick plan:
- Marcus and infra will look at runtime metrics and recent deploys (ETA 20–30m)
- We'll open an incident bridge and send a customer-facing status within 30 min
- If needed we'll fail over to the compatible model variant and throttle non-critical traffic to protect the payment flow

Can you confirm whether you can accept a short-term rate limiting policy (10–20% reduction) while we stabilize?

—Karthik
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:44 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency & 502s on inference calls

Karthik — please spin up an exec bridge (15 min cadence) and include product leadership. We need a short, factual status for Samir that sets expectations (root cause unknown yet, mitigation in flight, ETA for next update/timeboxed action).

Also: flag our SLA and credits policy to legal if they push; keep sales ops in the loop.

Laura
Head of Customer Success

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:35:17 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency & 502s on inference calls

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed sudden queue depth increase on pool-gpu-06 at ~08:12 PST.
- Correlated with a canary rollback that completed at 08:10 — appears some traffic routed to an older quantized variant that has a serialization mismatch causing lock contention.
- Error pattern: upstream 502s from runtime process when KV cache misses skyrocket; p95 CPU on host hit 98% and request timeouts start returning 502.

Immediate actions taken:
- Isolated affected hosts and began diverting traffic to pool-gpu-03/04.
- Restarted runtime on two hosts to clear stuck workers.
- Preparing a targeted rollback of the canary to force the newer variant.

I attached a quick screenshot of the dashboard with the spike (perf-dashboard-1130.png). ETA for full containment: 45–60 minutes depending on cache warming.

—Marcus
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@pegasus.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:50:02 -0800
Subject: Pegasus Analytics — immediate status and next steps

Samir — quick update from our side: we have an active incident and are in a bridge. Initial impact looks tied to a recent canary which routed some traffic to an older quantized model variant; that caused queueing and KV cache pressure, leading to elevated CPU and 502s.

What we're doing now:
- Diverting traffic off affected hosts and restarting stuck workers (in progress)
- Forcing a canary rollback to unify model variant routing (ETA 30–45m)
- If rollback doesn't reduce errors we will fail over to the previous compatible model and apply short-term rate limits to non-payment paths to protect your payment flow

Request: can Pegasus accept a temporary 15% reduction in non-payment traffic for up to 2 hours while we stabilize? That will help keep the payment verification path healthy.

Customer-facing status we will send in 30m: short cause summary + mitigation + ETA. We will follow up with a post-incident report and remediation actions.

Please reply to confirm whether the temporary rate limit is acceptable.

—Karthik

From: Samir Rao <samir@pegasus.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anika D'Souza <anika@pegasus.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:03:08 -0800
Subject: Re: Pegasus Analytics — immediate status and next steps

Karthik — thanks for the quick response and the transparency. We can accept the temporary throttling on non-payment traffic; please prioritize the payment flow.

Two asks: 1) keep this at the exec level — our CTO wants updates, 2) because this hit production, our procurement/legal team will likely seek a credit; please route that conversation through our account team.

We'll stand by for the 30-minute status.

Samir

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Exec update cadence & follow-ups for Pegasus incident

Team — well handled so far. Two asks from leadership:
1) Start a short exec bridge at 12:15 PST (15-min cadence) — include product, infra, sales lead, legal on invite; use bridge code INFRA-4592.
2) Karthik/Marissa — prepare a crisp customer note (1–2 bullet summary, mitigation, ETA for RCA and credits timeline) for Samir and his CTO.

I'll also open a tracking ticket in the incident board and request a preliminary RCA by EOD. Keep the customer updated every 30 minutes until contained.

Evelyn
VP, Customer Operations
